subject.title: Enhancement: Allow custom safe headers in fetch-guard cross-origin redirects

question: Should OpenClaw add an operator-controlled way to retain selected custom headers across cross-origin fetch-guard redirects, and should that policy be scoped by destination origin instead of a global safe-header list?
rationale: This deliberately relaxes a credential-forwarding boundary and adds public config surface, so automation cannot choose the acceptable trust model or guardrails.

options.title: Design a scoped operator policy
options.body: Allow custom header retention only with strict defaults, header-name validation, redirect-destination scoping, docs, and regression coverage.

options.title: Keep strict stripping only
options.body: Reject the new config surface and continue dropping credential-like custom headers on all cross-origin redirects.

options.title: Add the requested global list
options.body: Implement `additionalSafeHeaders` directly, accepting that any allowed header may be replayed to any cross-origin redirect target.

recommendation.title: Design a scoped operator policy
recommendation.body: Allow custom header retention only with strict defaults, header-name validation, redirect-destination scoping, docs, and regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The open question is whether to relax the strict redirect-header boundary he introduced.
